acceptance: The cause of each difference is traced to code and stated in the PR.
A test runs the same request through the CLI path and the MCP path at scale 0.01 and asserts equal config blocks, or asserts the documented, intended difference.
If the difference is intended, compare refuses or warns on the pair with the not-comparable exit code, and the MCP reference states it.
context:
Source: found on 2026-11-13 while delivering the agent-facing work (PRs BenchBox-dev/benchbox#4202, #4203 and BenchBox-dev/benchbox-site#152, #153, #154). Related: the earlier item cli-mcp-execution-type-divergence-still-live; check whether it already covers part of this. Guardrails: work in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight); never edit the primary clone. Related items share one feature branch and PR where their files overlap. No live-cloud runs and no credentials in Git or logs; heavy work only through lock-taking entry points or make heavy-run after make heavy-status. Follow the comment policy and add a changelog.d fragment for user-facing changes. Re-verify every cited file and line before acting; they are hints. Stop and report rather than widen scope.

Closeout (2026-11-14): https://github.com/BenchBox-dev/benchbox/pull/4228 merged (6bb08eb3b9). Cause: MCP built the benchmark without the CLI's resolved compression (so it generated uncompressed data) and built DatabaseConfig without registered platform defaults (DuckDB ran with a 12GB system-profile limit against the CLI's 8GB default). MCP now uses the same sources, read through core; real duckdb runs from both entry points record identical config blocks, pinned by tests/integration/test_cli_mcp_result_parity.py. DataFrame runs now record host-load start and end samples outside every timer. The 'saved_config' label actually means registered defaults plus overrides.
description:
Problem: for the same platform, benchmark and scale, a CLI bundle records compression zstd and the saved-config platform options, while an MCP bundle records compression none and no platform options (observed while proving seed and iterations equivalence for PR #4202). Results from the two entry points may therefore not be comparable, and the bundles say so only implicitly.

Outcome: either both entry points apply the same defaults, or the difference is intended, recorded and treated as a comparability dimension by compare.
